newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: Rice prices in the southern U.S. were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher in the week ended February 1, USDA Market News said in its weekly summary.

In the South, long grain milled rice prices sold mostly at $20.50 per cwt.; Medium grain traded mostly at $18.50-$19.00; Second heads were steady and Brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50-$15.75, the USDA said.
Southern rice by-products were lower, bran was $5.00-$12.00 lower and millfeed was steady to $3.00 lower.
In California, prices were steady and Medium grain sold mostly at $19.00-19.50 with some discounts down to $18.00.

Rice bran in California was steady. California ship loadings for week ended February 1, 1997, were as follows: at Stockton, CS Ocean loaded 8,900 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bagged rice and 1,099 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 bagged second, destination Japan. At Sacramento, the Stellar Glory and the Global Explorer loaded 10,000 tonnes each of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bagged rice, destination Japan. The Ist loaded 17,809 tonnes of medium grain rough rice, destination Turkey.
Inspections of California rice for export in the week ended February 1, totalled 1,054,475 cwt. The total since October 1, 1996, was 5,797,589 cwt, against 3,325,376 cwt a year earlier.
